rationale:
ROUND 4 of submission 7ef4de4e. Round 3 was 6 APPROVE / 2 object (editquality, bug_historian, reuse_agent, guidelines, guardian, improvement_guardian all approved). This round answers both objections; the three edits are unchanged in intent, with edit 3's SQL hardened.

1) render_guardian (HIGH, edit 1) — RESPECTFULLY REBUTTED WITH EVIDENCE, and one real adjacent risk it did not name is now disclosed.
The objection states scoped mode 'REGENERATES section HTML from content_data but SKIPS pages whose content hash is unchanged', which would make this fix a no-op since a template-only change leaves content_data identical. That sentence is real, but it is NOT from this code — it is quoted from the concept register (docs026_concept_register/register/styling-render-pipeline.md:389 and two .buckets copies). Against the actual implementation:
  (a) `grep -rn content_hash --include=*.go platform/ internal/` returns NO hit in rerender_page_sections_action.go, create_rerender_items_action.go or save_page_sections_action.go. The only content_hash users are rag_actions, code_symbols, vet_med_price_scrape and a struct field. There is no content-hash comparison anywhere in the page-rerender path.
  (b) The ONLY three skip paths in the re-render loop are enumerable and none is hash-based: component not found in schemas (line ~229), planSection status != 'ready' (~239), and empty html_template (~250). Each calls carryStoredSection and increments `carried`. A section with a loadable component, a ready plan and a non-empty template is re-rendered from htmlTemplate — which IS the changed template.
  (c) EMPIRICAL: probe item 478c44c9 (reason=section_data_resolved, this exact page) reached rerender_sections and processed it — section_count:1, escalated:true. Scoped mode engaged and did not skip on any hash; it stopped at the content pre-check, which is precisely what edit 2 fixes.
So the register entry is stale or wrong with respect to this code. I am flagging that separately as a defect in the register, because a reviewer citing it as fact produced a high-severity blocking objection against a correct plan — that is a real cost and it will recur.
  (d) THE RISK render_guardian DID NOT NAME, now disclosed: the planSection 'deferred' branch (plan_sections_action.go:1090-1108). For a component with an empty input_schema, planSection defers — and the section would be CARRIED, silently defeating this fix — when comp.Function contains 'article', 'content', 'body', 'text' or 'blog'. For tool-loot-table-balancer the function matches none, so it returns 'ready' and re-renders. But a future tool named e.g. 'tool-content-planner' WOULD be carried. Edit 2 does not address that; it is a real residual and belongs on the record rather than in a later surprise.

2) debug_historian (medium ×2 + low, edit 3) — ALL THREE ACCEPTED AND FIXED IN THE SQL.
  - The UPDATE is now gated on the pre-state marker (steps ? 'create_rerender_item'), so a re-run is a 0-row no-op per the needle-gate rule instead of reporting UPDATE 1 and bumping updated_at.
  - RETURNING now asserts post-conditions inline rather than describing them in a comment.
  - The sequencing hazard now carries an explicit VERIFY-AGAINST-THE-POD step: grep the running chassis binary for the new call site before applying 171, not git and not the image tag.

3) reuse_agent (low, edit 1) — markPagesPendingRebuild is now quoted with file:line the same way its sibling was, closing the asymmetry: it is pre-existing, not new machinery.

4) bug_historian (low, edit 1) — accepted, not changed: the helpers only logger.Warn on failure. That is store_generated_component's existing pattern and matching it keeps one behaviour for one mechanism; diverging here would be a second silent contract. Recorded as a known limitation of the shared pattern rather than fixed asymmetrically on this path.

--- ROUND 3 RATIONALE, RETAINED ---

ROUND 3 of submission 7ef4de4e. Round 2 was REVISE on a SINGLE medium objection from editquality, whose own note said: 'The one open thread is the compose_note rewire target, which should be a one-query confirmation before this goes from object to approve.' That query is now run and quoted in grounded_in. NOTHING ELSE HAS CHANGED — the three edits are identical to round 2 in intent and sketch.

THE ANSWER: compose_note DOES exist as a live step key on tool-improver, so the rewire target is real and edit 3 cannot produce the dangling next_step the objection feared. Live query: has_compose_note=t, has_append_note=t, compose_note.action=execute_llm_prompt, compose_note.next_step=append_note. Corroborated by the council's OWN round-1 read-only check, which printed compose_note's full config while answering a different question — the evidence was already in the trail.

ON bug_historian's STANDING OBJECTION (edit 2): it acknowledges round 2 is 'a genuine improvement' that 'directly answers the prior objection', but holds the underlying shape is unchanged — a shared guard special-cased per component class rather than declared required-vs-optional-but-expected intent made structurally explicit. I agree with that diagnosis and will not pretend this change fixes it. Making content intent structural means a schema contract change across 122 components plus the missingkey=zero root behind this guard: architecture work for a human decision, not a rider on a fix that unblocks a wholly broken delivery path. Recording it as accepted-and-deferred rather than quietly narrowing the guard again. What this change does guarantee is that the special case is now a NAMED, queryable marker (component_level='tool') instead of an inferred shape, so a future structural fix can find and remove every site of it with one query — which round 1's heuristic could not have offered.

--- ROUND 2 RATIONALE, RETAINED ---

ROUND 2 of submission 7ef4de4e (REVISE, objections from editquality and bug_historian). The diagnosis and the three targets are unchanged; every change below answers a specific objection, and one of them improved the design materially.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE ROUND 1:
(a) bug_historian objected that edit 2 exempted a BROADER set than the rationale justified: 'any schema with zero required llm fields' also covers components declaring OPTIONAL source:'llm' fields that were nonetheless expected to be populated — reopening a silent-drop path for a class I had never examined. Correct, and the objection's 'missing' note pointed at the right fix: use an EXPLICIT intent marker rather than a derived proxy. content_components already carries component_level, and the loot component is component_level='tool'. Edit 2 now keys on component_level=='tool' AND an empty input_schema. Measured effect: 12 of 122 active components, down from the 19 schemaless the reviewers sized in round 1 — the 5 schemaless 'section' and 2 schemaless 'site' components are no longer touched at all. This is a better fix than the one I submitted and it came out of the review.
(b) editquality objected that edit 1 rested on an unverified claim about createRerenderWorkItem stamping reason + component_id. Its body is now quoted verbatim in grounded_in.
(c) editquality flagged that componentIDStr/componentFunction did not appear in scope. They do (lines 86 and 110); round 1's sketch was over-abbreviated. Fuller context is now shown. No code change resulted — flagging it as a sketch defect, not a code defect.
(d) editquality objected that edit 3's jsonb path was unconfirmed against the live row. The council's own read-only check returned has_create_rerender_item=true, has_update_component=true, current_next_step='create_rerender_item'. That query is now embedded in the migration as a pre-flight.
(e) The reviewers' checks surfaced something neither I nor the objections stated outright: complete.config.output_fields still lists 'rerender_item', the removed step's output_field. Edit 3 now clears it too, so the rewire leaves no dangling reference. This is the round's most concrete catch.
(f) bug_historian's architecture flag is acknowledged and NOT addressed here: this pre-check exists as a downstream mitigation for the generic missingkey=zero rendering behaviour, which remains unpatched. This change further specialises an already-specialised guard. I accept that framing; the narrowing is now marker-based rather than heuristic, so it does not make the root harder to fix later, and the root is out of scope for a change I want to keep small.
(g) On 'every future caller of update_component_html inherits a side-effecting work item': accepted and intended. The action's entire purpose is 'the durable template changed', and requesting the re-render is the semantically correct consequence of that for ANY caller — it is precisely what store_generated_component already does. The alternative (each caller remembering to request it) is the bug being fixed.

ORIGINAL RATIONALE (unchanged): bugs_open/024. No tool-improver fix has EVER reached a live tool page. The loot-table benchmark has failed the same mobile-fit check across three repair cycles since 2026-07-17; each cycle wrote a good fix and reported success. The fixes are all in content_components.html_template; page_components.rendered_html is still 9,901 chars — the v1 born length — and the live page is byte-identical to birth. Re-verification could only ever come back RED: the page under test never changed. Three defects in series: (1) update_component_html only sets build_status='pending', which nothing scans; (2) tool-improver's create_rerender_item sets no spec_data, so the item carries no spec.reason and check_rerender_mode takes else_step -> rerender_single_page ('Simple concatenation - no template re-rendering'), assembling stale HTML and marking the page deployed; (3) forcing the correct branch proved (2) and exposed the last defect — rerender_sections RAN then ESCALATED, because the content pre-check refuses any section with empty content_data, which a self-contained tool has by design. check_escalated routes escalated==true -> complete, bypassing save_sections, the only writer of rendered_html. The render is computed and thrown away, and the page is escalated to a full rebuild that would regenerate and destroy the tool.

plan.summary: A fix written to content_components.html_template never reaches the rendered page. Make update_component_html REQUEST the re-render (reason=section_data_resolved + component_id) via the existing markPagesPendingRebuild/createRerenderWorkItem pair instead of relying on a build_status='pending' flag nothing reads; stop rerender_page_sections escalating sections whose component is explicitly marked component_level='tool' with no input contract (12 of 122 components), which currently discards a good render and requests a destructive full rebuild; and drop tool-improver's redundant, mis-keyed, reason-less create_rerender_item step together with the now-dangling 'rerender_item' output field.

edits.rationale: The action changes the durable template, so it is the correct place to request the re-render — exactly as store_generated_component does for the identical situation. Reuses that file's existing helpers rather than adding machinery: markPagesPendingRebuild performs the same UPDATE and additionally returns the affected site_ids, and createRerenderWorkItem raises a component-scoped item already stamped with the reason and component_id that check_rerender_mode and create_rerender_items both require. Blast radius is one step fleet-wide: update_component_html is used only by tool-improver.update_component (independently confirmed by the council's own round-1 check). Round 2: helper body now quoted in grounded_in; sketch shows that componentIDStr and componentFunction are already in scope.
edits.sketch:
--- a/platform/orchestration/actions/update_component_html_action.go
+++ b/platform/orchestration/actions/update_component_html_action.go
@@ context: both identifiers below are ALREADY in scope in this function @@
    line  86:  componentIDStr := inputs.Get("component_id")
    line  87:  componentID, err := uuid.Parse(componentIDStr)
    line 110:  var componentFunction string
    line 116:  `, componentID).Scan(&currentHTML, &componentFunction, &componentName)
 (round-1 objection was a misread of an over-abbreviated sketch; no rename needed)

@@ -248,15 +248,26 @@
-	// --- 4. Mark associated page_components as pending rebuild ---
-	// Do NOT set rendered_html here. ... The rerender pipeline regenerates
-	// rendered_html correctly; we just flag that it needs to run.
-	rebuildResult, err := params.DB.ExecContext(ctx, `
-		UPDATE page_components
-		SET build_status = 'pending', updated_at = NOW()
-		WHERE component_id = $1
-	`, componentID)
-	if err != nil {
-		logger.Warn("UpdateComponentHTMLAction: Failed to update page_components", zap.Error(err))
-	}
-	var pagesMarked int64
-	if rebuildResult != nil {
-		pagesMarked, _ = rebuildResult.RowsAffected()
-	}
+	// --- 4. Mark pending AND REQUEST the re-render ---
+	// build_status='pending' is INFORMATIONAL ONLY: nothing in the repo scans
+	// page_components for pending rows (store_generated_component_action.go:455
+	// says so in its own comment). Flagging alone is why every tool fix since
+	// 2026-07-17 stayed invisible on the live page. Reuse the exact pair that
+	// store_generated_component already uses for the identical situation.
+	//
+	// Reached only after the rowsAffected==0 guard above, so the request is
+	// raised only when the durable template actually changed.
+	pagesMarked, affectedSiteIDs := markPagesPendingRebuild(ctx, params.DB, componentIDStr, logger)
+	// createRerenderWorkItem stamps spec.reason='section_data_resolved' and
+	// component_id — the two fields check_rerender_mode gates on and that
+	// create_rerender_items requires to scope + stamp the per-page items.
+	// It keys per-component (component_regen_rerender:<id>), inserts at
+	// 'triaged', and does so via raw SQL, so it does NOT pass through
+	// insertWorkItem's two-strike rule (the rule that was marking the old
+	// tool-improver items 'unresolved' at birth).
+	for _, sid := range affectedSiteIDs {
+		createRerenderWorkItem(ctx, params.DB, sid, componentIDStr, componentFunction, "tool-improver", logger)
+	}

edits.rationale: ROUND 2 — rewritten to use an explicit intent marker instead of an inferred one, per bug_historian. The guard conflates 'has no stored content' with 'needs no stored content'. Rather than deriving that from schema shape (which would also exempt components declaring optional llm fields — the silent-drop path bug_historian correctly objected to), key on the library's own component_level='tool' marker plus an absent input contract. A tool is self-contained HTML with no LLM-authored content to lose, so the hazard this guard exists for cannot arise. Article-body protection is preserved bit-for-bit, and so is the behaviour of every schemaless section/site component. component_level is already loaded by loadSectionComponents and carried on componentInfo.Raw, so this needs no new query and no struct change. Without this edit a tool page can never be re-rendered at all, whatever the caller asks for.

Once edit 1 lands, this step is not merely redundant but harmful: it raises a SECOND item keyed site-wide (rerender_tool_fix_<domain>, create_work_item_action.go:128) with no spec.reason, which re-ships stale HTML, and which insertWorkItem's two-strike rule marks 'unresolved' at birth once two prior rerenders have completed — every such item since 2026-07-18 is unresolved in production. Round 2 adds the two things the reviewers found: the live-row pre-flight confirming the jsonb path, and removal of 'rerender_item' from complete.config.output_fields, which would otherwise dangle. Snapshot first, per the standing rule.

-- Idempotent: gated on the pre-state marker, so a re-run is a 0-row no-op
-- (needle-gate rule, debug_historian round 3) rather than a spurious UPDATE 1.
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(
      jsonb_set(
        default_config #- '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item}',
        '{workflow,steps,update_component,next_step}', '"compose_note"'
      ),
      '{workflow,steps,complete,config,output_fields}',
      '["tool_data","improved_html","update_result"]'
    ),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE type = 'tool-improver'
  AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND default_config->'workflow'->'steps' ? 'create_rerender_item'   -- <= needle gate
RETURNING
  NOT (default_config->'workflow'->'steps' ? 'create_rerender_item')        AS step_removed,
  default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'update_component'->>'next_step'     AS rewired_to,
  NOT (default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'complete'->'config'->'output_fields' @> '["rerender_item"]')
                                                                            AS output_field_cleared;
-- Expect exactly: t | compose_note | t   (one row; zero rows on a re-run)

-- Rewire target confirmed live BEFORE this migration (round-3 evidence):

-- compose_note.input_fields = [input_data, tool_data, update_result] — never

grounded_in: REBUTTAL EVIDENCE (render_guardian, round 3): `grep -rn "content_hash" --include=*.go platform/ internal/` — ZERO hits in rerender_page_sections_action.go / create_rerender_items_action.go / save_page_sections_action.go. plan.risks:
ROUND 4 — additions at 8-10.
ROUND 3 — unchanged from round 2 except where noted.
1) Edit 2 remains the judgement call, but is now marker-based and measured: exactly the 12 active component_level='tool' components with no input contract change behaviour. A lookup MISS (hasSchema=false) still escalates, and any component with a schema — including one declaring only optional llm fields — is completely untouched. Reviewers should still check that no component_level='tool' row is secretly relied upon to carry LLM content.
2) Edit 1 makes every update_component_html caller raise a rerender request. Today that is one caller; the inheritance is intended (see rationale (g)) but should be a conscious one.
3) createRerenderWorkItem defaults workItemSource to 'component-creator'; 'tool-improver' is passed so provenance stays honest. Confirm rerender-pages' claim path does not filter on source.
4) The whole chain rests on create_rerender_items propagating reason + component_id (create_rerender_items_action.go:136-140). If that coupling is changed, this fix silently reverts to assemble-only — worth a comment at that site.
5) SEQUENCING (unchanged and important): Go edits are inert until a chassis image ships; edit 3 is live immediately. Applying 171 BEFORE the image would remove the only (broken) rerender request and leave none at all. Image first, then 171.
6) Not fixed here, deliberately: insertWorkItem's two-strike rule counting 'complete' as a failed attempt (load_work_item_actions.go:1019) and create_work_item's site-wide item_key (create_work_item_action.go:128); and the generic missingkey=zero root behind this guard. All filed; none on this change's path.
7) ACCEPTED AND DEFERRED (bug_historian, standing): this special-cases a shared guard per component class rather than making required-vs-optional-but-expected content intent structural. Not fixed here; deliberately recorded rather than narrowed away. The marker is queryable (component_level='tool'), so every site of the special case is findable when that structural work is scheduled.
8) DISCLOSED RESIDUAL (not fixed): planSection defers an empty-schema component whose function name contains article/content/body/text/blog, which would carry rather than re-render it. Does not fire for this tool; would for a future 'tool-content-*'. Worth a follow-up, out of scope here.
9) render_guardian's round-3 blocker is rebutted on evidence, not waved away. If a reviewer can point at a content-hash skip that actually exists in the page-rerender path, this plan is wrong and should be rejected — I could not find one in code or in a live probe.
10) The concept register carries a stale claim about this pipeline that produced a high-severity objection. Filing that separately; noted here because it will mislead the next reader too.
